requirements: Implement the owner numerical model for multi-product advection, axial dispersion and interface tracking on the requested route and inlet schedule; do not relabel the EPANET dilute-water quality adapter as a product-batch solver.

Return source-bound time-by-position component fractions, density, dynamic viscosity, temperature and absolute pressure in the exact declared layout, with property package/version/basis and any CoolProp or reviewed mixture-model provenance.

Return total and per-component signed mass ledgers using initial + inlet - outlet - final + numerical_adjustment, and where thermal coupling is enabled return an independently checkable energy ledger without hiding closure in numerical adjustment.

Preserve phase, pressure reference, flow direction, boundary interpolation, geometry, clock, source and convergence meaning; unsupported phase change, mixing rules, pig interaction or reversal stays explicit.
acceptance_evidence_required: Piston-displacement, zero/finite-dispersion, constant-property and conservative multi-component limiting cases agree with independent arithmetic or analytic references, with mesh/time-step refinement and residual histories.

Every component and total mass ledger closes within caller-declared tolerances and component ledger terms sum to their total counterparts; energy closure is reported separately when heat transfer or variable properties are active.

Held-out experimental or operational interface arrival and contamination-width observations quantify error and applicability by product pair and operating regime; calibration rows are not reused as independent validation.
Changing source, geometry, inlet schedule, property model, boundary interpolation, grid or provider version invalidates replay receipts.

requests.title_ko: 펌프 정지 동특성·액체 MOC 동시 결합 계약
target_components: caller-owned pump and drive transient solver
requirements: Provide a versioned pump/drive transient API for trip and coastdown with signed four-quadrant flow, head or torque, angular speed, rotor inertia, drive torque, hydraulic torque, loss torque, check-valve state and convergence histories; do not derive time response from a static affinity point alone.

Couple the owner pump equations and the liquid MOC characteristic/node equations at the same accepted time level so flow and head are solved together rather than replaying a one-way prescribed trace as a coupled solution.

Return source-bound power histories and an independently checkable rotor energy ledger with initial/final 0.5*I*omega^2, drive work, hydraulic work, dissipated energy and bounded numerical adjustment.
Detect and type unsupported cavitation, column separation, reverse rotation, motor regeneration, check-valve impact and operating-map extrapolation without clipping them into the supported domain.
acceptance_evidence_required: Zero-inertia/quasi-steady, no-hydraulic-load, constant resisting torque, energy-conserving rotor and pump-trip limiting cases agree with independent analytic or arithmetic references across time-step refinement.

The simultaneous MOC/pump node residual, network volume balance, rho*g*Q*H power identity, torque-power identity and full rotor energy ledger each meet caller-declared tolerances without excessive numerical adjustment.

Independent pump coastdown or trip experiments provide synchronized speed, pressure/head and flow with inertia, fluid properties, sensor calibration and clock uncertainty; calibration and held-out validation runs remain separate.
Changing pump curve/map, inertia, drive/control logic, check-valve rule, fluid property, clock, source or solver version invalidates dependent receipts.
shared_invariants: signed flow/head/torque, angular speed, absolute pressure and energy sign conventions preserved
asset/scenario/clock/pump/drive/fluid/source/configuration and evidence bound to the response
unknown/unsupported/nonconverged stays explicit; no inferred cavitation safety, field accuracy or operating authorization
pump owner implements dynamics and drive physics; the consumer validates exchange and MOC coupling
